$meta.readThisFirst: This is a NEW global component finalized on Singh's 2026-09-03 request: 'we need to make a consistent global component for same so everywhere in the system we will use the same approach.' It is used as the left sidebar of a RECORD (Client, Caregiver, Staff, …): it shows who the record is and lets the user move between that record's sections. Singh ruled three scope points the same day — see the `RULED` markers on collapse (behavior.collapseExpand), the flat-list-with-header/divider-reserved-for-future (anatomy.navList), and single-or-multiple top actions (geometry.topActions). Per Singh's standing instruction on every contract — 'with every component you have complete behavioural and action related information and how it works, and what's the purpose' — the `behavior` and `purpose` blocks below are mandatory, not optional.

purpose: The left sidebar of any record in the product. It answers two things at once: WHO this record is — photo, name, timezone, address, email, phone, date of birth, office, and a shortcut to their notes — and WHERE you can go within that record — a list of its sections (for a Client: Main Details, Schedule, Clinical Evaluation, Billing…; each item opens that whole section). It is ONE component reused for every record type so the profile-plus-section-nav experience is identical everywhere. It collapses to a thin avatar-only rail to give the content area more room, and re-opens on a tap.

anatomy.panelContainerNote: A flex column, 240px wide, background sidebar/secondary-bg (#f8fafc). NO border and NO gap between the three sections — each section owns its own padding and they butt together on one continuous fill. The line seen against the white content area is the colour boundary between #f8fafc and surface/base, not a drawn border (confirmed: none set in Figma).

topActions.role: One or more icon actions for the record context. Measured instance: back (arrow_circle_left, filled circle) on the left, person_search (search users) on the right.
topActions.countRule: SINGLE or MULTIPLE — Singh, 2026-09-03: 'the top portion is the top actions which can be single or multiple.' Figma ships both a 'Single Action' and a '2 actions' variant.

blocks: identity: 70px round avatar (with a camera edit badge) + name (Heading/h5) + timezone (Fields/value)
contact rows (id_info): Address · Email · Phone · Date of birth · Office — each an 18px icon + a value
userProfileCard.linkRows: Address, Email and Phone render as blue actionable links (text/links, text/brand). Date of birth and Office render as static grey text (text/secondary).
userProfileCard.expandedCollapsed: Two variants: Expanded=Yes (full 240px card, 280px tall) and Expanded=No (collapsed 44px rail inside the card; in-context the whole panel is a 50px rail showing only a 40px avatar).

navList.role: The record's sections. Each item opens one whole section.
navList.arrangementRule: FLAT list of Nav Items for v1. Singh, 2026-09-03: 'the list also supported separator and header, that is for future — if case will come I will apply.' So Nav Header and Nav Divider are SPECCED and kept ready, but not rendered by default.

typography.note: No new type styles. Reuses Heading/h5 (name), Fields/value (timezone + contact values), Button/label (View Notes), Nav-item body (Inter Medium 14/16), Label/overline (future nav header).

colourFormula.pattern: Panel = sidebar/secondary-bg. Text splits three ways: text/primary (name, default nav item), text/secondary (timezone, DOB, office), text/tertiary (future header). Links = text/links (address, email) and text/brand (phone). Icons = icon/primary (top actions) and icon/soft (contact rows). Interactive nav item = action/soft/bg → action/ghost/hover → action/ghost/pressed, with action/ghost/text-hard on hover+active. View Notes = action/primary/bg + action/primary/text-neutral. Camera badge = action/secondary/bg + action/secondary/text. EVERY one resolves in the repo semantic layer with dark/hc/warm variants — verified 2026-09-03.

navSemantics.value: The nav list is a <nav aria-label> of real links/buttons; the current section carries aria-current="page" (this drives the Active visual, not a manual class).

collapsedExpandTrigger.value: Singh's rule is 'tap ANYWHERE on the rail to expand.' For keyboard users that whole-rail target must be a REAL focusable control (e.g. a <button aria-expanded aria-label="Expand profile"> wrapping the rail). A bare <div> click is mouse-only and fails WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1.

contactLinks.value: Address → map link, Email → mailto:, Phone → tel:. DOB and Office are plain text, not links. Leading icons are decorative (aria-hidden) — the text carries the meaning.

contrast.value: action/ghost/text-hard resolves to blue-700 in the repo, already contrast-verified 5.72:1 AA (token comment, _theme-light.scss:112). Nav-item hover/active text therefore passes on its grey backgrounds.

focusVisible.value: Every interactive element (top actions, View Notes, contact links, nav items, expand trigger, camera badge) needs a visible focus ring — do not remove the kit's :focus-visible outline.

defects: D1 — LAYER-NAME TYPOS in Figma: 'profiel navigation preview' (27325:70008) and 'profiel navigation cllapsed preview' (27331:70994) — 'profiel'/'cllapsed'. Cosmetic, but these become component names; flag to Figma AI for a rename before this is published as a library component.

D2 — RESOLVED 2026-09-04 (Singh ruling). NOT a whole-card link. WHEN EXPANDED, the card has multiple independent actions and EACH is individually clickable — View Notes, address (map), email (mailto), phone (tel), edit-photo. The Figma whole-card <a> is a prototype artifact, NOT the intent; do not wrap the card in a single link (that would be the nested-interactive conflict). WHEN COLLAPSED, only the avatar shows and the WHOLE rail is one tap target that expands the card — after which its individual actions are clickable. Singh, 2026-09-04, verbatim: 'the user profile side navigation has multiple actions so all are clickable when expanded. on collapse we are not showing any information but just the picture, at that moment the whole side bar (collapsed) is clickable and tappable which will expand the entire profile card with all details which is clickable.'

D3 — SINGLE-ACTION ALIGNMENT: the top-actions layout makes the leading action flex-1, which right-aligns any trailing action. For the 'Single Action' variant, confirm whether the lone action sits left (as the back button does) or is meant to be centred/right — the single-action variant's internal alignment was not separately measured.

D4 — HOVER vs ACTIVE ARE CLOSE: a hovered (non-current) nav item and the active (current) nav item share the identical blue text (action/ghost/text-hard); they differ ONLY by background — hover #f1f5f9 vs active #e2e8f0, two adjacent greys. On some monitors these are hard to tell apart, and a hovered item can momentarily look like the current one. Consider a stronger active affordance (e.g. a left accent bar or medium-weight bump) — none exists in Figma today.

D5 — LEGACY TOKEN NAMES in the variable payload: letter-spacing binds 'fonts/tracking/X-tracking-0' and 'fonts/tracking/X-tracking-neg-024' (X- legacy prefix), and a raw primitive 'Neutral (Light) / N500' #42526E appears. Same legacy-name cleanup already tracked system-wide — one Figma rename closes them; do not propagate the X- names into the build (the kit binds --ls-heading / semantic vars instead).

D6 — control/height-compact (=24, the View Notes min-height) is bound in Figma but, like control/height-default elsewhere, may be absent from the owner's variable export — same known export gap flagged on Button/Fields/DDM. Confirm it exists before treating 24 as a token rather than a literal.

D7 — 'Nav Project' (5847:8401, 40px) exists in the component set as a larger nav variant but was NOT measured (Singh deprioritized grouping to 'future'). Documented as existing; its exact styling must be read from Figma before it is used.

The single-action top-bar internal alignment (see D3).

collapseExpand.effect: The ENTIRE panel collapses to a ~50px rail showing only the avatar; tapping ANYWHERE on the rail re-expands it to the full 240px panel.
collapseExpand.source: Singh, 2026-09-03, verbatim: 'The profile entire side section is collapsible … and on tapping on anywhere on the side bar it will open again.'
collapseExpand.note: State is app-owned (add/remove --collapsed). The whole-rail tap target must be keyboard-reachable — see accessibility.collapsedExpandTrigger.

navItemClick.action: Click a section in the nav list.
navItemClick.effect: Opens that whole section of the record in the content area and marks the item Active (current). Only one item is Active at a time.
navItemClick.source: Singh, 2026-09-03, verbatim: 'each tab will unbox the entire section details.'

navItemStates.effect: Default = grey row, dark text. Hover = light-blue row, blue text. Active = deeper grey-blue row, blue text (the current section).

viewNotes.effect: Opens the person's notes. (In Figma the button links to the notes prototype flow.)

contactLinks.effect: Address opens a map, Email opens a mail composer (mailto:), Phone starts a call (tel:). Date of birth and Office are informational only, not tappable.
contactLinks.note: Standard conventions for these row types; the blue link colour in Figma confirms address/email/phone are actionable, DOB/office are grey/static.

editPhoto.action: Tap the camera badge on the avatar.
editPhoto.effect: Opens the change/upload-photo flow for this record.

topActions.effect: Back returns to the previous screen (the list the record was opened from); search (person_search) opens user search. The bar carries one action or several depending on context.
